interview_questions.question_text: Great start. How would this approach scale under 10x traffic, and what are the time or space complexities involved?

interview_answers.answer_text: React uses a Virtual DOM which is an in-memory javascript representation of real DOM nodes. When state updates occur, it computes a diff using a tree reconciliation algorithm. With React 18 Fiber, the diffing is broken into small chunks of work that can be paused, resumed, or aborted based on priority using useTransition, preventing the UI from freezing during heavy operations.

To avoid race conditions, we can use pessimistic locking like SELECT FOR UPDATE in SQL which locks rows until the transaction commits. Alternatively, optimistic locking uses a version number column; if the version has incremented when we try to commit, the query fails and retries. For microservices, we use distributed locks like Redis Redlock.

We connect users via WebSockets and use Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs) like Yjs or Operational Transformation (OT) to resolve conflicting text insertions and deletions deterministically across all peers. Deltas are stored in Postgres or Cassandra and periodic snapshots saved to S3.
